title: useImperativeHandle
summary: Let a parent call a small, deliberate set of actions on a child component.
nestedConcepts: Pass a ref through a component
Prefer declarative props for normal UI

subtopics.title: Understand what a ref stores
subtopics.explanation: A ref holds a value between renders without causing the component to render again when that value changes. Refs are useful for DOM nodes and imperative handles, not for values that must update the visible UI. State is the right choice when a change should trigger a render.

subtopics.title: Pass a ref through a component
subtopics.explanation: A ref stores a value without causing a render. A child can receive the ref and use useImperativeHandle to expose selected methods, such as focus or reset. React 19 allows ref as a prop; earlier versions commonly wrap the component with forwardRef.

subtopics.title: Expose a small imperative API
subtopics.explanation: `useImperativeHandle` lets a component decide what its ref exposes, such as `focus()` or `reset()`, instead of exposing the entire DOM node. Define the handle in the child and keep it narrow. This is useful for integrating with focus management or a third-party imperative library.

subtopics.title: Prefer declarative props for normal UI
subtopics.explanation: Use props and state for ordinary data flow, because they describe what the UI should show. A ref-based method is appropriate for a specific imperative action, such as focusing an input. If every parent operation needs a method, the component may need a clearer declarative API.

subtopics.title: Keep the handle narrow
subtopics.explanation: Expose only the operations a parent genuinely needs. A small handle keeps internal elements and state private, so the component can change its implementation later. Document when a method is available and avoid turning the ref into a second, hidden state-management system.

foundations.overview: A parent sometimes needs one small action from a child, such as focusing an input. useImperativeHandle customizes the value exposed through a ref. In React 19, a function component can receive ref as a prop; older React versions use forwardRef. Prefer props for ordinary communication.
foundations.mentalModel: It is like giving someone a remote with three useful buttons instead of handing over the machine controls.
foundations.whyItMatters: It keeps the public controls small instead of exposing every internal detail.
foundations.formalDefinition: useImperativeHandle customizes the value exposed through a ref. A ref is an object that lets code reach a DOM node or an imperative API. Most components should communicate through props; use this hook only when a parent truly needs an action such as focusing an input.

keyTakeaways: Expose a narrow handle only when a parent needs an imperative action.
Use props for normal data and event communication.
React 19 accepts ref as a prop; older versions use forwardRef.

codeLab.title: Expose one small action
codeLab.instructions: Build a text input component with a Focus button. Keep the DOM ref inside the input component and expose only a focus action to its parent.
codeLab.expectedOutput: The parent button can focus the child input. The child does not expose its full DOM implementation.
hints: Break the task into state, event handling, and rendered feedback.
Keep the interface accessible with labels and meaningful button text.
